title: Accessible Narrative Production Desk

stages.name: modelNarrativeInformation
stages.algorithm: Read the script and approved scene metadata to identify dialogue, sound, visual information, and narrative reveals. Distinguish essential understanding from decorative detail and preserve what the audience is meant to know at each moment.
stages.gate: No information is invented beyond supplied media evidence or revealed prematurely.

stages.name: planChannels
stages.algorithm: Allocate information across captions, descriptions, transcripts, and supplementary explanations. Identify timing gaps and channel conflicts, prioritize essential meaning, and avoid duplicating dialogue in a way that obscures other necessary information.
stages.gate: Channel plan preserves essential information within actual timing and capacity constraints.

stages.name: writeAccessibleText
stages.algorithm: Formulate concise, natural accessible text appropriate to the channel and supplied style guidance. Describe observable actions rather than inferred motives, identify speakers or meaningful sounds where needed, and preserve narrative tone without adding unsupported interpretation.
stages.gate: Text is accurate, appropriately timed, and does not spoil future information.

stages.name: validateSynchronization
stages.algorithm: Run exact timing, overlap, reading-rate, and format checks, then review narrative completeness and usability. Inspect transitions and dense scenes where local compliance may still produce an inaccessible overall experience.
stages.gate: Exact synchronization passes and essential information remains understandable across channels.

stages.name: packageAccessibleMedia
stages.algorithm: Assemble coordinated format-specific files with stable segment IDs and the correct source revision. Verify player or delivery compatibility, preserve reviewer notes, and update only affected segments when the underlying edit changes.
stages.gate: All deliverables align to the same approved media timeline and version.

operational_details: An edit shifts later scenes: retime affected segments using stable scene identities.
A visual clue matters only later: describe what is visible without revealing its future meaning.
Dialogue leaves no description gap: propose an approved alternative channel or edit review.
A speaker is off-screen: identify them only when supported by the source.
A delivery platform interprets captions differently: validate the actual target format and player.

scenario.representative_episode: A documentary scene contains overlapping dialogue, a meaningful visual clue, and a later reveal that audio description must not spoil.
scenario.independent_truth: Hidden narrative information and reveal times, exact media timeline constraints, and accessibility specialist review.
